title: AI for private equity: what are PE-backed companies using it for?
description: For operators of PE-backed companies: where AI pays first, revenue as well as cost. Named results sponsors published, the rules and who signs off.
verdict: Most portfolio companies are early: about a third use AI day to day, and many are still piloting.[^1][^2]
Sponsors aim AI at revenue more than cost: pricing, dormant accounts and missed calls, not just back-office savings.[^1][^3]
Start from the value creation plan, and give each AI use one measured revenue or cost number.[^4][^5]
Clean data comes first: data quality and readiness top the barriers mid-market and PE leaders name.[^6][^7]
People keep the decisions: most PE leaders require human checks on AI agent output.[^8][^5]

headings.ranked: Where does AI pay first in a PE-backed company?
headings.rules: Which rules apply to AI at a PE-backed company?

summary: AI in a PE-backed company is software that drafts, sorts, predicts or answers inside daily work, from calls to the close.[^11][^12] It drives the earnings growth sponsors now need from operations, not higher sale multiples.[^10] Clean data and an owner tied to the value creation plan make or break it.[^6][^4]
humanRole: Sales leaders approve price changes and AI-drafted offers before a customer sees them. Three in four asset management and PE leaders require human validation of AI agent output, and 56% aren't comfortable with fully autonomous agents.[^8][^9]

Your service manager owns the dispatch board: at IFS, agents propose schedules and the dispatcher approves them.[^13] Granite Comfort keeps staff in the loop on AI-handled after-hours calls, per its vendor.[^14]
Your controller signs the close and the board pack, even when AI drafts them. Operating partners mostly want supervised autonomy (41%) or autonomy only on low-stakes tasks (38%).[^5]
Your COO owns the list of AI uses and decides what goes live. The free AI Risk Management Framework from NIST, the federal standards body, gives the steps: govern, map, measure, manage.[^16]
HR keeps every hiring decision. California and Colorado rules from 1 Jan 2027 give people an appeal or human review of significant AI decisions.[^17][^18]

ranked.name: Pricing, quoting and margin
ranked.why: Price and margin optimization is a top AI revenue priority for 47% of the PE leaders FTI surveyed.[^1] In BDO's survey of 400 US PE firms, pricing is a main value lever for 15%, rising to 16% next year.[^21]
ranked.payoff: Price realization and gross margin per order, plus quote turnaround time.

ranked.name: Dormant accounts and sales follow-up
ranked.why: At Apollo's Univar Solutions, a chemical distributor, an AI sales agent re-engaged dormant accounts with 30% engagement in a pilot.[^3] At Blackstone's Renaissance Learning, a lead model doubled average order value in a pilot.[^19]
ranked.payoff: Accounts reactivated, and pipeline won from the dormant list.

ranked.name: Missed calls and booking, for service businesses
ranked.why: Granite Comfort, a heating, cooling and plumbing platform, says AI books over half its bookable calls; its pilot brand grew revenue 20% (vendor's case).[^14][^15] Customer support is among the most common portfolio company uses in L.E.K.'s 2026 survey.[^11]
ranked.payoff: Answered-call rate, booked jobs and after-hours revenue.

ranked.name: Procurement and spend
ranked.why: IT and procurement are the top AI cost priorities, each named by 48% of PE leaders.[^1] Apollo found price gaps on the same items across companies, and one company cut procurement cost over 65% with contract AI.[^22][^3]
ranked.payoff: Spend under contract, duplicate vendors and savings at renewal.

ranked.name: Month-end close, financial planning and the board pack
ranked.why: Financial planning and analysis (FP&A) is the most common portfolio AI use, named by 55%.[^12] Of operating partners, 83% run at least one AI agent in finance work, led by loan covenant checks at 58%.[^5]
ranked.payoff: Days to close, hours per board pack, and variances flagged before the board meets.

ranked.name: Answers for field technicians
ranked.why: At Apollo's Barnes Group, an industrial firm, AI search of product specs gave technicians fast answers and a 5x return in year one.[^3] IFS, an EQT-backed software firm, sells dispatch agents that schedule 300,000+ technicians, with dispatcher review.[^13]
ranked.payoff: Time to answer a technician's question, and first-time fix rate.

ranked.name: Add-on acquisitions: diligence and integration
ranked.why: Of UK private capital firms surveyed, 92% use AI in due diligence.[^23] FTI-Andersch found 27% use it for financial due diligence and 13% for sale preparation.[^24]
ranked.payoff: Weeks from closing an add-on to one set of books, customers and price lists.

ranked.name: Value creation plan tracking
ranked.why: Bain advises starting from the value creation plan and aiming AI at three to five big uses.[^4] Only 38% of operating partners measure AI's revenue or margin impact.[^5]
ranked.payoff: Share of AI uses with a measured revenue or cost number.

ownData.title: Which named companies have sponsors shown AI results for?
ownData.intro: We found published AI results for ten named portfolio companies; only three are clearly not software businesses, and two of those three are revenue wins.[^3][^14] Every row is a result the sponsor published, or a source quoting the sponsor or a named vendor. Non-software wins sit in sales, calls and technician answers, jobs a distributor or service business already runs.[^3][^15]
rows: Heating, cooling and plumbing services, not software[^15]
Over half of bookable calls booked by AI; pilot brand revenue up 20% year over year (vendor's case)[^14]
Average order value doubled in a pilot[^19]
Costs down 40% in some content work and 15% in care[^30]
From about one policy a week to ten a day[^31]
About $2M a year saved per customer, sponsor-reported[^30]
Sold at 95%+ and 60%+ above book value[^28]
ownData.note: Zavient count from sponsor sites, sponsor-quoted press and one vendor case, pulled 26 Nov 2026. Results are self-reported, not audited, and mix pilots with scaled use. Large sponsors dominate because they publish most; this ranks no firm.

rules.name: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) private fund adviser rules
rules.what: No SEC quarterly-statement rule applies.[^32] Investors still ask for the same data through templates from the Institutional Limited Partners Association (ILPA), so expect standard data requests from your sponsor.[^45]

rules.name: SEC predictive data analytics proposal
rules.what: There is no AI-specific conflict rule for advisers.[^33] SEC exam priorities for 2027 still list AI use, per a law-firm summary.[^39]

rules.name: AI washing: SEC and Federal Trade Commission (FTC) enforcement
rules.what: The SEC settled false AI claims with two advisers for $400K in total, and issued an order against Presto Automation.[^34][^35] The FTC's Operation AI Comply targets deceptive AI claims.[^37] Overstated AI in a sale deck can surface in buyer diligence.[^38]

rules.name: SEC Regulation S-P amendments
rules.status: Compliance from 3 Dec 2025 (larger firms) and 3 Jun 2026 (smaller)
rules.what: Applies to SEC-registered advisers, so mostly to your sponsor.[^36] It requires an incident response program and customer notice, which reach any AI vendor touching investor or customer data.[^36]

rules.name: EU AI Act, as amended by the 2026 Digital Omnibus
rules.status: In force; hiring and credit-scoring rules from 2 Dec 2027
rules.what: Applies if you sell AI-enabled products in the EU or use AI on people there.[^40][^41] Transparency duties started 2 Aug 2026; the Omnibus, in force 27 Jul 2026, moved high-risk rules to 2 Dec 2027.[^40][^42]

rules.name: California CCPA rules on automated decision-making technology (ADMT)
rules.status: In effect 1 Jan 2026; ADMT duties from 1 Jan 2027
rules.what: For significant decisions about jobs, credit, housing or health, you owe notice, an opt-out or a human appeal, and a risk assessment.[^17][^43]

rules.name: Colorado SB 26-189
rules.what: Replaces the 2024 Colorado AI Act and keeps a right to human review of consequential AI decisions.[^18]

rules.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 42001
rules.what: A common backbone for an AI policy and list of uses.[^16] ISO/IEC 42001 is the certifiable standard for an AI management system, if a buyer asks for one.[^44]

rules.name: ILPA Reporting Template v2.0
rules.status: Industry standard for funds launched from 1 Jan 2026
rules.what: Not law, but it shapes the data your sponsor asks you for.[^45] A refreshed Portfolio Company Template is due in Jan 2027.[^46]

watchOuts: No measured number, so no proof: only 38% of operating partners measure revenue or margin impact.[^5] Set one revenue or cost number per use before the pilot starts.

Pilots that never reach the profit and loss (P&L): MIT researchers found 95% of generative AI pilots showed no P&L return.[^48] Tie each pilot to the value creation plan, as Bain advises, then scale it or stop it.[^4]
Dirty data stalls AI: mid-market firms name data quality as the top barrier, and PE leaders name data readiness.[^6][^7] Clean customer, item and price data before buying any AI tool.
Scaling without a playbook: 41% of operating partners do it, and 63% of portfolio companies have informal guidance only.[^5] Write a one-page AI policy and a list of uses, each with an owner.[^16]
AI washing in the exit story: the SEC and FTC have acted on false AI claims.[^34][^37] Claim only what you measured, and keep the evidence for buyer diligence.[^38]
Staff left behind: 85% of mid-market leaders say executives are keener on AI than their staff.[^49] Train the people who use it, and frame it as help with their work.

faq.q: Do private equity firms hire consultants for AI?
faq.a: Yes: half of UK private capital firms surveyed bring outside AI specialists into their portfolio companies.[^23] In RSM's mid-market survey, 52% use outside consultants for AI now and 37% plan to.[^6]

faq.q: How is AI being used in private equity?
faq.a: PE firms use AI mostly on deal work: 92% in due diligence, 84% in sourcing and 78% in monitoring and investor reporting.[^23] Inside portfolio companies, FP&A leads at 55%, followed by sales, customer support and procurement.[^12][^1][^11]

faq.q: Is AI actually paying off in portfolio companies?
faq.a: Only partly so far: 19% of GPs see positive net returns now, and 40% expect them within a year.[^26] Bain and StepStone found 39% of GPs expect no material financial impact in 2026.[^25]

faq.q: Where should a portfolio company start with AI?
faq.a: Start from the value creation plan and pick three to five high-value uses, revenue as well as cost.[^4][^1] Give each one owner and one number to move before the pilot starts.[^5]

faq.q: Does the SEC regulate AI in private equity?
faq.a: Not with an AI-specific rule: the SEC withdrew its predictive data analytics proposal in June 2025.[^33] It still examines AI use, and has settled false AI claims with advisers.[^39][^34]

faq.q: How much are PE firms spending on AI in portfolio companies?
faq.a: More each year: 80% of GPs say portfolio AI spending rose last year, and 39% raised it by 25% to 49%.[^26] Among mid-market firms, 84% expect AI spending to rise.[^6]

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy for standard work: 76% of enterprise AI uses are now bought, up from 53%.[^47] Granite Comfort bought a call-booking product, and Apollo shares vendors across its companies.[^14][^3] MIT researchers found bought tools succeed about twice as often as internal builds.[^48]
buyVsBuild.build: Build, or configure on top of what you own, where your data is the edge: pricing from order history, dormant-account lists, product spec libraries.[^3] Bain says the big wins come from company data tied to the value creation plan.[^4]

pickElse: Your sponsor runs a central AI team, as Blackstone, Hg and Apollo do: use it first.[^20][^28][^3]
One standard workflow, such as payables or call answering: buy the feature in your enterprise resource planning (ERP) system or a point tool.[^47]
You need ongoing AI leadership, not a project: consider a fractional chief AI officer. Only 9% of operating partners have an AI center of excellence.[^5]
Data is the blocker: clean master data in your ERP or business intelligence tool before any AI.[^6]

answers.human-role: People keep the decisions: sales leaders approve prices, service managers own dispatch, the controller signs the close, and the COO decides what goes live.[^8][^13][^5]
answers.ranked: AI pays first in revenue work: pricing, dormant-account follow-up and missed-call booking, then procurement and the finance close.[^1][^3][^14]
answers.rules: No AI-specific SEC rule applies to your company; the rules that bite are state AI laws, the EU AI Act if you sell there, and AI-washing enforcement.[^33][^17][^40][^34]
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI goes wrong when nobody measures it, pilots never reach the profit and loss, data is dirty, or sale materials overstate it.[^5][^48][^6][^34]
answers.buy-or-build: Buy for standard jobs such as call answering, payables and contract review; build only where your own data is the edge, such as pricing.[^47][^4]
answers.something-else: Pick something else when your sponsor has a central AI team, the job is one standard workflow, you need a part-time leader, or data is the blocker.[^20][^47][^6]

offer.heading: Which AI job pays back first at your company?
offer.body: Usually a revenue job: pricing, dormant accounts or missed calls, then procurement or the close. In a free 30-minute call we rank your top two against your value creation plan, with one number to move for each.

reviews.notes: Dana (COO): clear on what to do first and who decides. Flagged jargon in the finance item: 'agentic finance use' and 'covenant monitoring'. Now reads 'AI agent in finance work' and 'loan covenant checks'. Value creation plan left as is; every PE-backed COO works to one.

Ops head: wanted to know a person still owns AI-handled calls. The Granite Comfort line now says staff stay in the loop on AI-handled after-hours calls (vendor's case). Dispatch and technician items keep ops measures: answered-call rate, first-time fix rate.

GM: revenue leads, which matches the P&L view. Both pricing and dormant accounts linked to the sales analytics guide, which is about who to call, not price. Pricing now links to the value creation plan guide, which works out what a point of price is worth; the VCP tracking item drops its duplicate link.

Controller (finance division head): the close item measured days and board pack hours but not what the board cares about. Payoff now adds variances flagged before the board meets. Head of sales: approval of AI-drafted offers before a customer sees them is stated in the human-role block.

Steve: the title starts with the search phrase, so the description now opens 'For operators of PE-backed companies' to say who it is for. FAQ 3 answers 'is it paying off' straight, with numbers. No Zavient price, per site rules; the offer stays the free 30-minute call.
